passage:
Kiran: Papa checked my bank statement again. Asked why there were two cafe charges 😔
Salma: Ugh. Is he going to stop your allowance?
Kiran: He said "if you can't explain, I'll hold next month's". I nearly told him it was for books.
Salma: Did you?
Kiran: No. I stopped myself. Lying would only make it worse.
Salma: True. What if you propose a budget? Rent, food, fun, all fixed?
Kiran: And send him a monthly sheet so he doesn't need to check? That could work.
Salma: And the freelance editing idea?
Kiran: Starting it this week. Then the cafe is my own money 😅
Salma: Good plan.

qa.q: What did Papa ask about on the statement?
qa.a: Why there were two cafe charges.

qa.q: Why did Kiran nearly say the charges were for books, and why did Kiran stop?
qa.a: Kiran feared losing next month's allowance, but realised that lying would only make things worse.

qa.q: What plan do Kiran and Salma come up with?
qa.a: A fixed budget for rent, food and fun, a monthly sheet sent to Papa, and freelance editing to earn Kiran's own money.

qa.q: How might Kiran's father see the monthly sheet?
qa.a: He may feel reassured and see less need to check the statement, since his checking probably comes from worry about money.

grounding: Kiran's parents track spending and hold the allowance as leverage; Kiran negotiates a clear budget, shares information and builds own income.
